meta.title: Arya Kavian — Software Engineer
meta.description: Software engineer and tinkerer working across web, AI, security and systems. Curious about what happens underneath.

hero.name: Arya Kavian
hero.intro: I build software, take it apart, and try to work out why it held together in the first place.
hero.imageAlt: An engraved tarot plate: Arya Kavian holding a laptop, between a starry night sky and a storm cloud, surrounded by books, crystals and foliage.

about.title: The character sheet
body: I'm a software engineer interested in the space between building things and understanding them. My work runs through web development, backend systems, infrastructure, AI and security — usually because something wouldn't stop bothering me.
Outside of code I'm drawn to things with character: old cars, photography, mechanical objects, and the occasional card trick.
Different subjects, same question. How does it work?

suits.title: The four suits
suits.intro: Everything I work with falls into one of four piles. The pile matters more than the logo.

items.name: Storms
items.line: Containers, reverse proxies, queues, CI, the machine underneath the machine.

items.name: Night sky
items.line: Building software around models, and asking hard questions about what they produce.

items.name: Crystals
items.line: Authentication, static analysis, vulnerability detection. How systems fail, and why.

items.name: Foliage
items.line: The part people actually touch. Interfaces that behave like well-made objects.

work.title: Things I built
work.note: Each one started as a question
work.intro: I needed something. So I built it. The interesting part was usually somewhere in the middle.
work.empty: No cards on the table yet.

writing.title: The codex
writing.intro: Notes from things I couldn't stop wondering about.

photos.title: Outside the terminal
photos.intro: Cars. Cameras. Machines. Things with interesting mechanisms.
photos.empty: Nothing developed yet. Come back after the next roll.

contact.title: Correspondence
contact.intro: Working on something strange, technical, or both? I read everything.

trick.hint: Go on. It's not a real trick.
lines: You didn't pick this card. It picked you.
The bug was in the middleware. It's always the middleware.
Every abstraction is a promise someone else has to keep.
It worked on the first try. Be suspicious.
The oldest machine in the room is usually the best documented.
Read the source. The docs are a rumour.
If you can't break it, you don't understand it yet.
Cache invalidation. That's the whole card.
